transcript:
Header:
- Date: 2026-04-14
- Time: 16:30 PT
- Duration: ~52 minutes
- Attendees: Jamie (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Logan (TidalWorks Head of Partnerships), Cara (CTO), Devon (Solutions Architect)

Summary (auto): quick triage and handoff of co-sell pipeline; agree on pilot scope and security artifacts to share.

00:00 Jamie Ortiz: hey everyone, thanks for joining — I'll kick us off, welcome Logan, Cara, Devon. we wanted to run through the two top co-sell opportunities and make sure we're aligned on technical blockers and GTM motion.
00:18 Logan Perez: yeah thanks Jamie, appreciate it. quick context — TidalWorks has a couple of deals where our channel execs think Redwood could be a differentiator for low-latency inference and the co-sell ask is to help with intro + technical credibility.
00:34 Priya Raman: great, can you name the accounts? that'll help us map people.
00:40 Logan Perez: sure — Account A is OceanRide (logistics, heavy on edge devices), Account B is HarborBank (fraud detection). Both are mid-enterprise, procurement cycles about 60–90 days depending on security gating.
01:02 Cara Liu: hi, i just wanna flag HarborBank is strict on data residency and SOC 2 type II, they also want SSO with SAML and want to see audit logs and key custody details.
01:16 Jamie Ortiz: totally, that's expected. Priya — on our side, we have Hosted API, Dedicated, and Private (VPC) options; for HarborBank sounds like Private w/ KMS or Dedicated with customer-managed keys.
01:31 Priya Raman: yeah. also we can propose a hybrid: run inference in TidalWorks' VPC with our control plane, or on Dedicated capacity with customer keys depending on OPA and procurement. note: there might be some confusion on terms — I heard "Sam-el" earlier — it's SAML.
01:50 Devon Smith: ha, yeah. from infra standpoint, HarborBank will require tls+mtls between services, and they want no token retention. how does Redwood handle KV cache and prefix caching? any concerns for PII?
02:06 Priya Raman: we do automatic prefix/KV caching but it's configurable — we can disable KV cache for sensitive routes and we have options to not persist logs beyond X days. our KMS integrations support bring-your-own-key in Dedicated and Private.
02:28 Logan Perez: good, that's helpful. pricing question — what kind of discount range should we expect for co-sell deals? their procurement asks for 20–30% list off the bat.
02:40 Jamie Ortiz: typical approach is we model a partner discount stack: channel rebate + committed volume. 20% is doable on larger pilots if there's a committed ARR motion; but also we can trade some discount for a longer committed period or reserved capacity.
02:58 Cara Liu: also we need to understand latency SLOs — OceanRide has 150ms p95 target for inference. can Redwood meet that in a hosted model?
03:12 Priya Raman: depends on model and region. hosted in-region usually hits that for trimmed models; for strict p95 you might prefer Dedicated pools in the same region or edge proxies. there's also quantization options; though coarse quant can affect quality.
03:36 Logan Perez: ok so for OceanRide maybe we propose a Dedicated pool with autoscale and burst?
03:44 Jamie Ortiz: yes, and we can include a fallback to hosted smaller models if dedicated capacity spikes. that's our graceful degradation pattern.
03:55 Devon Smith: on the technical ask: can we run a perf benchmark? we can provide a representative prompt set and token lengths.
04:02 Priya Raman: absolutely — we'll run a benchmarking harness. ideally you share sample prompts, sequence lengths, and concurrency targets. we'll do two runs: hosted and dedicated.
04:16 Logan Perez: timeline wise, procurement for HarborBank could be stickier — they want security docs first. can you send SOC2 + network diagram + a short HLD?
04:27 Jamie Ortiz: yes, Priya will compile and send the security pack. we'll also add a short diagram for the VPC flow.
04:34 Cara Liu: thanks. one more on compliance — do you offer audit log retention limits by tenant?
04:40 Priya Raman: yes, retention is configurable in Private and in Dedicated we can extend retention as an add-on. hosted has default retention windows but we can negotiate for enterprise customers.
05:00 Jamie Ortiz: moving to next item — who owns post-close support? we suggested TidalWorks handle first-line support for accounts you bring in and Redwood provides technical escalation and SRE for infra issues; is that acceptable?
05:15 Logan Perez: that works — we want to own account relations but rely on Redwood for deep technical escalations.
05:24 Devon Smith: practical note — for the pilot let's scope 3 weeks of integration and 4 weeks of live run, with weekly checkpoints. success metric for HarborBank is false positive rate reduction of X% and latency p95 < 200ms.
05:40 Priya Raman: we'll propose a pilot SOW: deliverables, data handling, and evaluation prompts.
05:49 Jamie Ortiz: quick competitive note — CloudServeAI is pushing a lower price but they don't have the Private deployment options in-region that HarborBank requires. AuroraEndpoints is also in deals but they have less transparent latency profiles.
06:08 Logan Perez: good to call that out.
06:12 Cara Liu: ok let's walk through the two accounts quickly and decide who to prioritize.
06:18 [short pause, people consult notes]
06:35 Logan Perez: prioritize HarborBank (A) because procurement windows open earlier; OceanRide (B) is next but they require more edge config.
06:45 Jamie Ortiz: agreed. action: Redwood to send tailored pilot scope for HarborBank and include a pricing band with a partner discount path.
06:55 Devon Smith: question — for HarborBank, do you require schema changes to logs or can we pipe logs to your endpoint via our collector?
07:04 Priya Raman: we can ingest via standard collectors; prefer newline-delimited JSON for events. we'll share an ingestion spec.
07:18 Logan Perez: also — legal ask: proof of KMS integration and key rotation policy.
07:25 Priya Raman: we'll include our KMS integration doc; note: BYOK flows are slightly different between Dedicated and Private, we'll highlight that.
07:40 Jamie Ortiz: great. next, pricing structure thought: we propose a 3-month pilot at a trial rate, then convert to reserved capacity at a commit that nets a 20% discount; additional partner rebate applied after a 12-month milestone.
08:00 Cara Liu: HarborBank will likely push for shorter pilot and no upfront commit. can we offer a pilot that doesn't require full commit but has an option to convert at a discount?
08:12 Jamie Ortiz: yes that's common — pilot-to-commit conversion. we'll include both options in the pricing sheet.
08:25 Logan Perez: ok, on internal ownership: Logan will be primary partner owner; Jamie will be Redwood AE; Priya will lead technical. Cara/Devon are the customer's tech leads.
08:40 Jamie Ortiz: perfect. any blockers we're missing?
08:46 Devon Smith: one: network firewall rules — HarborBank will restrict outbound to a handful of endpoints. do you support static IP allowlisting?
08:55 Priya Raman: yes, for Dedicated we can provide egress IP ranges; for Private deployed in their VPC, it's all internal. we'll include a network diagram and list of endpoints.
09:12 Logan Perez: can we get a quick risk call script for execs? like: what happens if latency spikes or service degrades in the pilot.
09:22 Jamie Ortiz: we'll provide an incident playbook snippet and an escalation matrix.
09:30 Cara Liu: perfect.
09:35 [10:00 minute mark: more granular triage of the pilot scope — checklist-style]
19:40 Jamie Ortiz: looping back — I'm going to summarize next steps and then we'll open for questions.
19:48 Jamie Ortiz: summary: Jamie send GTM one-pager and pricing sheet; Priya send security pack + ingestion spec + IP ranges; Devon share sample prompts & traffic profile; Logan coordinate introductions to HarborBank procurement.
20:05 Logan Perez: timeline — we target pilot kick by 2026-05-04, with a conversion decision by 2026-06-01 if metrics are met.
20:15 Cara Liu: that timeline is aggressive but feasible if legal gets the docs quickly.
20:25 Jamie Ortiz: ok, we'll aim to deliver docs by 2026-04-17.
20:32 Devon Smith: small nit: for OceanRide edge cases we'll propose a lower-latency model quant but we'll include evals because quality might drop.
20:45 Priya Raman: noted.
21:00 [crowd crosstalk, confirming calendar invites]
21:22 Jamie Ortiz: any final questions?
21:28 Cara Liu: none here. just want to make sure we get the SAML SSO flow documented.
21:34 Priya Raman: yes — we'll include a SAML SSO appendix.
21:40 Logan Perez: thanks everyone — excited to move this forward.
21:46 Jamie Ortiz: thanks, we'll follow up with the items we discussed.
21:52 [meeting ends]
notes: References: GTM one-pager (link), security packet (link), pilot SOW template (link), benchmarking harness spreadsheet (link). These were referenced and will be shared via email and CRM.
